name: Gavrilo Princip — The Assassin

choices: Look up at the car — confirm what you are seeing before you do anything
Step back against the wall — put more distance between yourself and the road while you think
Your hand moves to your coat — not a decision yet, only a reflex, the body ahead of the mind
opening.narrative: The corner of Franz Josef Street and the Appel Quay is quiet compared to the main boulevard — the crowd here is thinner, the brass band more distant, the smell of the river stronger. You have been standing with your back to Schiller's window for long enough that the shopkeeper glanced at you twice through the glass before losing interest. The cough rises and you press it down. Somewhere on the quay the cheering has started again, which means the motorcade is moving. You are not watching the road. You are watching the cobbles. Then the sound of the engine changes.

briefing: The dry cough has been with you all morning and you have been swallowing it, pressing it down under the noise of the crowd, because a man standing alone and coughing draws eyes. Your coat is too heavy for the late-morning warmth but you cannot take it off. The FN presses cold against your ribs through the lining. You have been standing at this corner for two hours in the belief that you were a soldier of a cause, and for the last forty minutes you have been standing here in the knowledge that the cause has failed — that Čabrinović's grenade bounced and detonated behind the Archduke's car, that the motorcade continued, that the others along the quay did nothing, that you yourself did nothing when it passed you, because it was moving too fast and the angle was wrong and then it was gone. You are thinking about leaving. You are thinking about the cyanide capsule in your left pocket and whether this is the moment to use it, or whether you will simply walk back to your room and wait to be arrested, which you expect will happen by evening. The morning is warm and smells of chestnuts. Then you hear the engine note of a large car changing — slowing — turning — and you look up.
description: You are nineteen years old, consumptive, and you believed it was over. The mission failed. The Archduke is alive. You are standing at a corner with a loaded pistol and nowhere to go — and then the car turns onto your street.
perspective: Write from the perspective of a nineteen-year-old nationalist who believes with complete sincerity that he is a soldier of liberation — not a murderer, not a terrorist in his own understanding, but a man striking a blow for the freedom of his people from an occupying empire. His conviction is real and must be rendered from inside without endorsement. The moral weight of what he does — and of what follows from it, twenty million dead — must be present in the writing without being imposed as a judgment on him in the moment. He does not know about the twenty million. He knows about Bosnia.
bridge_sentence: [DRAFT] The chestnut smoke is drifting the wrong direction now.
character_hooks: I positioned myself at this corner this morning because the turn from the quay is tight and slow — I thought it would give me the best angle if the motorcade came back this way. I did not expect it to.
The cough has been worse this week — I have been coughing blood, which I have told no one, and my hands are less steady than I want them to be.

Danilo Ilić told me before the mission that if Čabrinović failed, I should not attempt anything alone — that a failed second attempt would be worse for the cause than no attempt at all. I have been thinking about that instruction for the last forty minutes.

defining_moment.setup: Čabrinović is on the steps by the Latin Bridge, soaking wet, and two policemen are standing over him — you can see him from here, which means this is what failure looks like and it is still happening. Ilić told you: if Čabrinović fails, do not attempt anything alone. You have been making and unmaking that instruction for forty minutes against Schiller's green-painted sign while the morning simply continued. The cough rises again, pressing upward, and your hands are less steady than you want them to be. Your left pocket holds the capsule. The pistol against your ribs has nothing between the hammer and the round but your own decision. Four meters. The car has stopped. Everything the world has just made simple is asking whether Ilić was right.

options.text: Ilić was wrong — the cause does not wait for a better moment than this.
Honor what Ilić told you — let the car pass and face what comes after.
Your left hand goes to your pocket — this is what the capsule was always for.

context_sentence: You are Gavrilo Princip, a failed assassin with a loaded pistol, and the Archduke's car is slowing in front of you.

inventory: FN Model 1910 semi-automatic pistol — loaded, .380 ACP, no external safety

startingKnowledge: That Čabrinović's grenade failed — you heard the explosion and watched the motorcade continue without stopping
The positions of all seven conspirators along the quay — you know who was stationed where and that none of them acted after Čabrinović
That the FN Model 1910 you carry is loaded, with no external safety engaged
That the cyanide capsule in your left coat pocket is your escape if you are seized — you have not yet decided whether you will use it
